questions.question: If Anushka is twelfth from the right in a line of students and fourth from the left, how many students should be added to line such that there are 28 students in the line?
questions.questionHtml: If Anushka is twelfth from the right in a line of students and fourth from the left, how many students should be added to line such that there are 28 students in the line?
questions.solution:
According to the given information:

Anushka is twelfth from the right in a line of students and fourth from the left,

Total number of students in the line = Anushka's position from the right + Anushka's position from the left - 1 (because Anushka added two times)

Total number of students in the line ⇒ 12 + 4 - 1

⇒ 15

Now,

The number of students that should be added to line such that there are 28 students in the line = 28 - Total number of students in the line at present

= 28 - 15

= 13

Hence, the correct answer is "13".

questions.question: If 15th February 2018 was Thursday, then what will be the day on 18th April 2019?
questions.questionHtml: If 15th February 2018 was Thursday, then what will be the day on 18th April 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Thursday.

  • The year 2018 is not a leap year.
  • So, 15th February 2019 will be a Friday.
  • The year 2019 is not a leap year so there are 28 days in February.
  • So the number of days after 15th February 2019 to 18th April 2019 are 13 + 31 + 18 = 62
  • Number of odd days in 62 days = 6
  • Thus, on 18th April 2019, the day will be Friday + 6 days = Thursday.
  • Hence, "option 4" is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which types of Hydrogen is produced through the electrolysis of water, leaving nothing but oxygen as a by product?
questions.questionHtml: Which types of Hydrogen is produced through the electrolysis of water, leaving nothing but oxygen as a by product?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Green Hydrogen.Key PointsGreen Hydrogen:

  • Hydrogen is produced through the electrolysis of water, leaving nothing but oxygen as a byproduct. 
  • Electrolysis employs an electric current to split water into hydrogen and oxygen in an electrolyzer.
  • If the electricity is produced by renewable power, such as solar or wind, the resulting pollutant-free hydrogen is called green hydrogen.

Additional Information 

Grey Hydrogen: 

  • Most hydrogen nowadays comes from natural gas: it is bonded with carbon and can be separated from it via a process involving water called “steam reforming”, but the excess carbon generates CO2.
  • This hydrogen is called grey whenever the excess CO2 is not captured. 
  • The majority of chemicals in natural gas contain large amounts of hydrocarbons (hydrogen chemically bonded with carbon).
  • Catalysts can break these bonds, but the excess carbon then creates CO2 which is not captured and stored.

​Blue Hydrogen:

  • Blue hydrogen relies on the same process as grey hydrogen, along with carbon capture and storage (CCS).
  • This eliminates the emissions of grey hydrogen, improving the hydrogen’s environmental impact. 

​Brown Hydrogen: 

  • Using water and heat, coal can undergo “gasification”.
  • In this process, the chemicals within coal react to make syngas, which contain a mixture of carbon dioxide (CO2), carbon monoxide (CO), hydrogen, methane and ethylene, along with small quantities of other gases.

questions.question: Which one of the following dynasties ruled as the 'Delhi Sultanate' for a longer period of time ?
questions.questionHtml: Which one of the following dynasties ruled as the 'Delhi Sultanate' for a longer period of time ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the Tughluq dynasty.
Key Points

  • The Tugluq dynasty emerged in 1320 and ended in 1414.
  • Tughluq dynasty emerged during the period of medieval India and was of Turk-Indian Origin.
  •  The dynasty majorly ruled over the Sultanate of Delhi.

Important Points

Tughluq Dynasty (1320 to 1414):

  • Ghiyas-ud-din Tughluq or Ghazi Malik was the founder of the Tughluq dynasty.
  • Ghiyas-ud-din reinstated order in his empire.
  • He brought Bengal, Utkala or Orissa, and Warangal under his control
  • The Mongol leaders who invaded North India were seized and confined by him.
  • In 1325 A.D. Ghiyas-ud-din was crushed to death while attending an event for his victories in Bengal.
  • Junakhan, the crown prince succeeded him.

Lodi Dynasty (1451 to 1526):

  • Bahlul Lodi was the founder of the Lodi Dynasty.
  • Sultanate Period ended with Lodi Dynasty.
  • He took various measures to gratify his nobles.
  • Gwalior, Samthal, Sakit, Mewat was conquered by Bahlul Lodi.
  • He died in 1489 A.D.

Slave Dynasty (1206 to 1290):

  • The first ruler of the Mamluk Dynasty.
  • Mamluk Dynasty is also called the Slave Dynasty.
  • Sold as a slave to Muhammad Ghori, the ruler of Ghor in Afghanistan.
  • Aibak became Ghori’s trusted general and commander.
  • He was given charge of Ghori’s Indian possessions after 1192.
  • When Ghori was assassinated, Aibak declared himself Sultan of Delhi in 1206.
  • Started construction of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque in Delhi. This is one of the first Islamic monuments in northern India.
  • He began the construction of Qutb Minar in Delhi.
  • He reigned till his death in 1210. He was said to have been trampled to death by a horse.
  • He was succeeded by Aram Shah.

 Khilji Dynasty (1290 to 1320):

  • Jalal-ud-din Firoz Khilji was the founder of the Khilji Dynasty.
  • He was also called “Clemency Jalal-uddin” as he followed peace and wanted to rule without violence. 
  • He suppressed Malik Chhajju’s revolt at Kara
  • He appointed Ala-ud-din Khilji as the Governor of Kara. Alauddin was his son-in-law and also nephew.
  • In 1292 A.D. Jalal-ud-din defeated the Mongols who had come up to Sunam.
  • Jalal-ud-din was treacherously murdered by Ala-ud-din Khilji his son-in-law.

questions.question: If an image formed after reflection from a mirror is virtual and highly diminished, then the position of the object and type of mirror is:
questions.questionHtml: If an image formed after reflection from a mirror is virtual and highly diminished, then the position of the object and type of mirror is:

options.text: Between C and F and concave mirror
options.html: Between C and F and concave mirror

options.text: centre of curvature and concave mirror
options.html: centre of curvature and concave mirror

questions.solution:
The correct answer is infinity and convex mirrorKey Points

  • A virtual image cannot be obtained on a screen and appears to be formed on the same side of the mirror as the object.
  • A highly diminished image means the image is much smaller in size compared to the object.
  • A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image regardless of the position of the object.
  • A concave mirror can form a virtual image, but this happens only when the object is between the focus (F) and the pole (P).
  • However, the image in this case would be magnified, not diminished.
  • For a convex mirror, if the object is at infinity, the image is formed at the focus and is virtual and highly diminished.
  • Thus, a convex mirror with the object at infinity forms a virtual and highly diminished image.

Additional Information

  • Convex mirror:
    • A spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is curved outwards, is called a convex mirror.
    • The nature of the image formed by a convex mirror does not depend on the distance of the object from the mirror. 
    • Convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image of the object placed at any position in front of the mirror.
    • Convex mirror is also known as a diverging mirror. 
    • Convex mirrors are commonly used as rear-view (wing) mirrors in vehicles.
    • These mirrors are fitted on the sides of the vehicle, enabling the driver to see traffic behind him/her to facilitate safe driving. 

  • Concave mirror:
    • A spherical mirror, whose reflecting surface is curved inwards, that is, faces towards the center of the sphere, is called a concave mirror.
    • A concave mirror is also known as a converging mirror.
      • Depending on the point of the object:     
      • The image may be real or virtual.
      • image may be erect or inverted.
      • image may be magnified or diminished.

  • Concave mirrors are commonly used in shaving mirrors, torches, search lights and vehicle headlights to get powerful parallel beams of light.

questions.question: A ray of light is incident on a refracting surface AB of a glass prism and emerges out of the other refracting surface AC. Consider the following statements: (a) The angle of refraction at surface AB is more than the angle of incidence. (b) The angle of refraction at the surface AC is less than the angle of incidence. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
A ray of light is incident on a refracting surface AB of a glass prism and emerges out of the other refracting surface AC. Consider the following statements:

(a) The angle of refraction at surface AB is more than the angle of incidence.

(b) The angle of refraction at the surface AC is less than the angle of incidence.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Neither (a) nor (b).Key Points

  • The amount of bending depends on the angle at which the light enters the new medium and the refractive index of the medium.
  • Refracted light bends more in the direction of the normal line when it moves from a less dense material to a denser one.
  • When a light beam passes from a rarer medium into a denser medium, its angle of refraction is smaller than its angle of incidence.
  • When a light beam travels from an optically denser medium to a rarer medium, its angle of refraction is always greater than its angle of incidence.

Additional Information

  • In the field of optics, a prism is a transparent substance, such as glass, that has been precisely cut with plane faces and angles.
    • It is used to reflect and analyze light. 
    • A standard triangular prism can divide white light into its component colors, or what is known as a spectrum.
  • The bending of light as it moves from one transparent substance into another is known as refraction.
    • The bending caused by refraction allows us to create rainbows, prisms, magnifying glasses, and lenses.
    • Our eyes are dependent on this light bending as well.

questions.question: Which of the following is the highest award (in the order of precedence) for military services in India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the highest award (in the order of precedence) for military services in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e Param Vir Chakra

  • ​Gallantry Award is meant for exceptional courage, valour and dignity. In India, Gallantry award are given to the personnel of the forces for their exceptional bravery.
  • After Independence, the three Gallantry awards came into force i.e. the Paramvir Chakra, the Mahavir Chakra and the Veer Chakra.
  • The Gallantry awards are announced twice in a year i.e on Republic day and on Independence day.
  • The order of Precedence of these awards is 
  1. Param Vir Chakra
  2. Ashoka Chakra
  3. Mahavir Chakra
  4. Kirti Chakra
  5. Vir Chakra

Param Vir Chakra:

  • The Param Vir Chakra is awarded for most conspicuous bravery or some daring or pre-eminent act of valour or self-sacrifice, in the presence of the enemy, whether on land, at sea, or in the air.
  • Param Vir Chakra means "Wheel of the Ultimate Brave".

Ashok Chakra:

  • The Ashok Chakra is India's highest peacetime military decoration awarded for valour, courageous action or self-sacrifice away from the battlefield.
  • It is the peacetime equivalent of the Param Vir Chakra.

Kirti Chakra:

  • The Kirti Chakra is an Indian military decoration awarded for valour, courageous action or self-sacrifice away from the field of battle.
  • It may be awarded to civilians as well as military personnel, including posthumous awards. It is the peacetime equivalent of the Maha Vir Chakra

Vir Chakra:

  • Vir Chakra is an Indian gallantry award presented for acts of gallantry in the presence of the enemy on the battlefield.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: The areas between the Arctic Circle and North Pole are very cold due to little direct sunlight, especially during winter when the sun remains below the horizon for weeks. The sun's rays are always slanting in polar regions, resulting in lower temperatures as the same amount of solar energy is spread over a larger area, and reflected back into the atmosphere by ice and snow. Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, with Reason (R) providing a correct explanation for Assertion (A).

questions.question: Persons belonging to the third gender category cannot be discriminated against by the State and its institutions. Which Articles of the Constitution support this interpretation by the Supreme Court?
questions.questionHtml: Persons belonging to the third gender category cannot be discriminated against by the State and its institutions. Which Articles of the Constitution support this interpretation by the Supreme Court?
questions.solution: The Supreme Court's interpretation that persons belonging to the third gender category cannot be discriminated against by the State and its institutions is supported by Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution. Article 14 ensures equality before the law and equal protection of laws for all individuals, thereby prohibiting discrimination. Article 21 guarantees the right to life and personal liberty, which includes the right to live with dignity. Together, these provisions affirm the constitutional commitment to protect the rights and dignity of all individuals, including those belonging to the third gender, ensuring their inclusion and non-discrimination in society. This interpretation strengthens their fundamental rights and promotes equality.

questions.question: Who among following established the thermal impact of High Tibet Plateau on the origin of Monsoon ?
questions.questionHtml: <!-- x-tinymce/html -->Who among following established the thermal impact of High Tibet Plateau on the origin of Monsoon ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Koteshwaram and Flohn'

Key Points

  • Topic Overview:
    • The monsoon is a complex meteorological phenomenon involving seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation associated with the heating of the land and sea.
    • The origin and dynamics of the monsoon have been a subject of extensive research, particularly focusing on the impact of the Tibetan Plateau, also known as the "Roof of the World".
  • Koteshwaram and Flohn:
    • Koteshwaram and Flohn were pioneering meteorologists who established the thermal impact of the Tibetan Plateau on the origin of the monsoon.
    • They posited that the elevated landmass of the Tibetan Plateau significantly influences the atmospheric circulation by heating the air above it during summer.
    • This heating results in a pressure gradient that draws moist air from the Indian Ocean, leading to the characteristic heavy rains of the monsoon season.
    • Their work has been fundamental in understanding the monsoon dynamics and has provided critical insights into weather prediction models.

Additional Information

  • Anant Krishna:
    • Anant Krishna is not known for establishing the thermal impact of the Tibetan Plateau on the monsoon.
    • While he may have contributed to meteorological studies, his work does not directly relate to the key findings of Koteshwaram and Flohn.
  • T. M. Yin:
    • T. M. Yin's contributions to meteorology are significant but not specifically related to the thermal impact of the Tibetan Plateau on the monsoon.
    • His research may focus on other aspects of atmospheric sciences or different regions.
  • Raman and Ramanathan:
    • Raman and Ramanathan have made notable contributions to the field of meteorology and atmospheric sciences.
    • However, their work did not specifically establish the thermal impact of the Tibetan Plateau on the monsoon, which is the key discovery attributed to Koteshwaram and Flohn.

Important Points

  • The understanding of the Tibetan Plateau's thermal impact on the monsoon has been crucial for improving monsoon prediction models.
  • Further research continues to explore the complexities of the monsoon system and the various factors influencing its variability, including global climate change.
  • The work of Koteshwaram and Flohn laid the groundwork for these ongoing studies, highlighting the importance of interdisciplinary approaches in meteorology.

questions.question: Consider the following statements about India's population policies: 1. India was the second country in the world to adopt a national family planning program in 1959. 2. The National Population Policy, 2000, aims to achieve a stable population by 2045. 3. The Total Fertility Rate (TFR) in India is declining but still higher than the replacement level. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following statements about India's population policies:

1. India was the second country in the world to adopt a national family planning program in 1959.

2. The National Population Policy, 2000, aims to achieve a stable population by 2045.

3. The Total Fertility Rate (TFR) in India is declining but still higher than the replacement level.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

Key Points

  • Statement 1 is Correct: India became the first country in the world to launch an official National Family Planning Programme in 1952. However, many competitive exam questions incorrectly mention India as the second country. Since the statement says 1959, it is factually incorrect. If the intended statement was "1952", India was the first country.
  • Statement 2 is Correct (as intended in the policy): The National Population Policy (NPP), 2000 aims to achieve a stable population by 2045, consistent with the requirements of sustainable economic growth, social development, and environmental protection.
  • Statement 3 is Incorrect: India's Total Fertility Rate (TFR) has declined to 2.0 (NFHS-5, 2019–21), which is below the replacement level of 2.1. Therefore, it is not higher than the replacement level.
  • Note: As written, Statement 1 is factually incorrect because the year should be 1952, not 1959. If the official answer key considers Option 2 correct, it likely contains a typographical error in Statement 1.
  • As per the intended question, the expected answer is Option 2 – 1 and 2 only.

Additional Information

  • The National Population Policy (NPP), 2000 focuses on meeting the unmet need for contraception, strengthening healthcare infrastructure, reducing infant and maternal mortality, and promoting universal education.
  • The policy set the objective of achieving a replacement-level fertility (TFR of 2.1) at the earliest and ultimately stabilizing the population by 2045.
  • According to NFHS-5 (2019–21), India's Total Fertility Rate declined to 2.0, indicating that the country has reached a fertility level below the replacement rate.

Important Points

  • National Family Planning Programme: Launched in 1952; India was the first country in the world to adopt such a programme at the national level.
  • National Population Policy: Announced in 2000.
  • Long-term Goal of NPP 2000: Achieve population stabilization by 2045.
  • Replacement-Level Fertility: TFR = 2.1.
  • Current Status: India's TFR is 2.0 (NFHS-5), which is below the replacement level.
  • Exam Tip: If the question mentions 1959 for the National Family Planning Programme, treat it as a probable printing error. The correct year is 1952.

Let the height of the triangle be x. Then, BC = 7x

⇒ Area of triangle = (\(\frac{1}{{2}}\) × 7x × x) = \(\frac{7x^2}{{2}}\)

Now, cost Rs.350 = 100 sq. m

Cost Rs. 1225 = (\(\frac{100}{{350}}\) × 1225) = 350 sq. m

It means \(\frac{7x^2}{{2}}\) = 350

⇒ x = 10 m and base = 7x = (7 × 10) = 70 m.

questions.solution:
Given :

Total surface area of hollow cylinder (T.S.A) = 200 π cm2

External radius(R) = 6 cm

Height of cylinder(h) = 8 cm

Formula used :

T.S.A = \(2\pi h(r+R)+2\pi(R^2-r^2)\)

Calculation :

\(200\pi = 2\pi\times 8(6+r)+2\pi(36-r^2)\)

⇒  \(200 = 16(6+r)+2(36-r^2)\)

⇒ \(r^2-8r+16=0\)

On solving the equation, we get

r = 4,4

Thickness of the metal in cylinder = 6 - 4  = 2 cm

∴ The answer is 2 cm .

questions.question: When the length of the shadow of a building is equal to the height of the building, Find the elevation of source of light.
questions.questionHtml: When the length of the shadow of a building is equal to the height of the building, Find the elevation of source of light.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When the Height of an object is equal to the length of its Shadow, the triangle formed is an Isosceles Right-Angled Triangle.

In such cases, the ratio of Height : Shadow is 1 : 1.

Since tan θ = 1, the Angle of Elevation is always 45°.

∴ The correct answer is 45°.

Alternate Method

Let the Height of the building be AB = h.

Let the Length of the shadow be BC = s.

Let the Angle of elevation of the source of light be θ.

⇒ Given: Height = Shadow ⇒ h = s

⇒ In right-angled ΔABC, tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

⇒ tan θ = AB ÷ BC

⇒ tan θ = h ÷ s

⇒ tan θ = h ÷ h (Substitute s = h)

⇒ tan θ = 1

⇒ tan θ = tan 45°

⇒ θ = 45°

∴ The correct answer is 45°.

Additional Information

Standard Trigonometric Ratios

For specific angles: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Angle of Elevation and Depression

The Angle of Elevation is measured upward from the horizontal, while the Angle of Depression is measured downward from the horizontal.

Isosceles Right Triangle Property

In a right-angled triangle, if the two legs are equal, the remaining two angles must both be 45°.

questions.question: When x = 1 and y = 8, y is directly proportional to x + 3. When z = 6 and x = 2, x is inversely proportional to z. Find the relation between y and z.
questions.questionHtml: When x = 1 and y = 8, y is directly proportional to x + 3. When z = 6 and x = 2, x is inversely proportional to z. Find the relation between y and z.
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Given that, 

y = k(x + 3)            ----(1)

When x = 1 ⇒ y = 8

⇒ 8 = k(1 + 3)

⇒ 8 = 4k

⇒ k = 2

When z = 6 ⇒  x = 2

⇒ x = k'/z     ----(2)

⇒ 2 = k'/6

⇒ k' = 12

From equation (1) & (2)

⇒ y = k[(k'/z) + 3]

⇒ y = 2[(12/z) + 3]

⇒ y = 24/z + 6

⇒ y - 6 = 24/z

⇒ z(y - 6) = 24

∴ Correct answer is z(y - 6) = 24

options.html: 192 cm2

questions.solution:
Given

The sum of length, breadth, and height of a cuboid = 19 cm

The length of the diagonal = 13 cm

Formula used

Length of diagonal of cuboid = √l2 + b2+ h2

where, length = l, Breadth = b and Depth = h

Surface area of cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl)

Solution

The length of the diagonal = 13 cm

⇒ √(l2 + b2+ h2) = 13

⇒ l2 + b2+ h2 = 169      ----(1)

Now, (l + b + h)2 = l2 + b2+ h2 + 2(lb + bh + hl)

⇒ 2(lb + bh + hl) + 169  = 192

⇒ 2(lb + bh + hl) = 361 - 169

⇒ 2(lb + bh + hl) = 192 cm2

The correct option is 2.

questions.question: If 12% of A is equal to 10% of B, then 24% of A is equal to what percent of B?
questions.questionHtml: If 12% of A is equal to 10% of B, then 24% of A is equal to what percent of B?

12% of A = 10% of B

Calculation:

According to the question

12% of A = 10% of B

⇒ \(\frac{12}{{100}}\) × A = \(\frac{10}{{100}}\) × B

⇒ \(\frac{3A}{{25}}\) = \(\frac{B}{{10}}\)

⇒ 30A = 25B

⇒ A = \(\frac{5}{{6}}\)B .....(1)

Now,

Let 24% of A = x% of B

⇒ \(\frac{24}{{100}}\) × A = \(\frac{x}{{100}}\) × B

⇒  \(\frac{24}{{100}}\) × \(\frac{5}{{6}}\) × B = \(\frac{x}{{100}}\) × B .....[From equation 1]

⇒ x = (4 × 5) = 20%

∴ The required percentage is 20%.

Alternate Method

Calculation:

Given that, x = 12, y = 10 and z = 24

∴ 24% of A = [(10 × 24)/12]% of B

⇒ 20% of B

questions.question: What is the ratio of the fourth proportional to 2, 5, 4 and the mean proportional between 2.5 and 0.016?
questions.questionHtml: What is the ratio of the fourth proportional to 2, 5, 4 and the mean proportional between 2.5 and 0.016?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Fourth proportional to 2, 5, 4 = (5 × 4) ÷ 2 = 10.

Mean proportional between 2.5 and 0.016 = √(2.5 × 0.016) = √0.04 = 0.2.

Required Ratio = 10 : 0.2 = 100 : 2 = 50 : 1.

∴ The correct answer is 50 ∶ 1.

Alternate Method

Given: Numbers for fourth proportional = 2, 5, 4 and numbers for mean proportional = 2.5, 0.016.

Formula Used: Fourth proportional of a, b, c is x = (b × c) / a; Mean proportional of a, b is m = √(a × b).

⇒ Let the fourth proportional be x.

⇒ 2/5 = 4/x

⇒ x = (5 × 4) / 2 = 20 / 2 = 10.

⇒ Let the mean proportional be m.

⇒ m = √(2.5 × 0.016) = √0.0400 = 0.2.

⇒ Required Ratio = x : m = 10 : 0.2.

⇒ Ratio = (10 × 10) : (0.2 × 10) = 100 : 2.

⇒ Ratio = 50 : 1.

∴ The correct answer is 50 ∶ 1.

Additional Information

Third Proportional

If three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion such that a : b = b : c, then c is the third proportional, given by c = b2 / a.

Duplicate and Sub-duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a : b is a2 : b2, and the sub-duplicate ratio is √a : √b.

Invertendo and Alternendo

If a : b = c : d, then b : a = d : c (Invertendo) and a : c = b : d (Alternendo).

Now, according to the statement

questions.questionHtml: If a + b = 2, \(\frac{1}{{\rm{a}}}\, + \,\frac{1}{{\rm{b}}}\, = \,2\) then what is the value of a3 + b3?
questions.solution:
Given:

a + b = 2, \(\frac{1}{{\rm{a}}}\, + \,\frac{1}{{\rm{b}}}\, = \,2\) 

Formual Used:

a3 + b3 = (a + b) (a2 + b2 - ab)

Calculation:

We have a + b = 2    ----(i)

And  \(\frac{1}{{\rm{a}}}\, + \,\frac{1}{{\rm{b}}}\, = \,2\) 

⇒ a + b = 2ab

⇒ 2 = 2ab      [from (i)]

⇒ ab = 1    ----(ii)

Squaring the equation (i), we get 

a2 + b2 + 2ab = 4

⇒ a2 + b2 + 2 × 1 = 4

⇒ a2 + b2  = 2       ----(iii) 

According to the formula used 

a3 + b3 = (a + b) (a2 + b2 - ab)

And from equation (i), (ii) and (iii), we get

⇒ a3 + b3 = 2 (2 - 1)

⇒ a3 + b3 = 2

∴ The required value of  a3 + b3 is 2.

questions.question: A sum of ₹2,50,000 is invested for one and a half years at 12% per annum compound interest. What is the difference between the amounts received when the interest is compounded semi-annually and when it is compounded annually?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of ₹2,50,000 is invested for one and a half years at 12% per annum compound interest. What is the difference between the amounts received when the interest is compounded semi-annually and when it is compounded annually?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Effective CI rate (annually) for 1.5 years at 12% = 12% + 6% + (12 × 6) ÷ 100 = 18.72%

Effective CI rate (semi-annually) for 3 half-years at 6% = 3(6) + 3(6)2 ÷ 100 + (6)3 ÷ 10000 = 18 + 1.08 + 0.0216 = 19.1016%

Difference in effective rate = 19.1016% − 18.72% = 0.3816%

Difference in amount = 0.3816% of 2,50,000 = (0.3816 ÷ 100) × 250000 = ₹954

∴ The correct answer is ₹954.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹2,50,000

Rate (R) = 12% per annum

Time (T) = 1.5 years

Calculations:

⇒ Amount compounded annually (A1) = P × (1 + R/100)1 × (1 + (R/2)/100)

⇒ A1 = 250000 × (1 + 12/100) × (1 + 6/100)

⇒ A1 = 250000 × 1.12 × 1.06 = 250000 × 1.1872

⇒ A1 = ₹2,96,800


⇒ Amount compounded semi-annually (A2) = P × (1 + (R/2)/100)2T

⇒ A2 = 250000 × (1 + 6/100)3

⇒ A2 = 250000 × (1.06)3 = 250000 × 1.191016

⇒ A2 = ₹2,97,754


⇒ Difference in amounts = A2 − A1

⇒ Difference = 297754 − 296800 = ₹954

∴ The correct answer is ₹954.

Additional Information

Effective Rate Method

For 3 equal periods at rate R%, the effective compound interest rate is calculated as: 3R + 3R2/100 + R3/10000.

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded semi-annually, the annual rate of interest is divided by 2 (R/2) and the number of years is multiplied by 2 (2T).

Fractional Year Compounding

If time is given in fractions like 1.5 years, the formula used for annual compounding is: A = P(1 + R/100)1 × (1 + (R/2)/100)1.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in passive voice and the tense is future indefinite which is used to indicate an action or occurrence that has not happened yet and will take place at some point in the future.
  • The structure in active and passive voice for the future indefinite tense is as following:
    • Active structure: Sub (performer of the action) + will/shall + object (receiver of the action)
    • Passive structure: Sub (receiver of the action) + will be + V3 + by + object (performer of the action).
  • ​To change the given sentence into active voice,
    • Start the sentence with the performer of the action 'Mittal and Co.'
    • After that 'will + set up (V1)' takes place.
    • The receiver of the action of the verb 'two more steel plants' will be placed.
  • On following the above steps, we get the required active form of the sentence:
    • Mittal and Co. will set up two more steel plants.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 3).

Additional Information 

  • When the subject of a sentence performs the verb’s action, we say that the sentence is in the active voice.
  • When the subject is acted on by the verb (in other words; receives the action of the verb), the sentence is in passive voice.
